It is also applied topically, as is bull bile with two <term>oboli</term> <gloss>small units of weight</gloss> of opium. Fumigation with stag hair is beneficial for the womb. It is reported that when hinds feel they are pregnant, they swallow a small stone, which is found in their excrement or in the womb (for it is found there too), and if tied on, it aids the delivery. Small bones found in the heart and womb are also very useful for pregnant women and those in labor. For we spoke of the pumice stone found in the uterus of cows in the same way in the section on the nature of cattle. Wolf fat applied topically softens the womb. It is even useful against harmful topical applications, and it is beneficial. Or if the delivery is beginning, it should be placed near the woman. So much so that it is even effective against harmful topical applications. And truly, the same is a remedy for afterbirth. There is a great use of the hare for women. Dried hare lung, when drunk, aids the womb. For fluxes, the liver with Samian earth drunk in water. For the afterbirth, rennet. They avoid baths the day before. Applied also with saffron and leek juice, and placed on wool, it expels dead fetuses. If hare wombs are consumed in food, they are thought to cause the conception of males. This is also achieved by their testicles and rennet. A hare’s conception removed from the uterus is said to bring lasting fertility to those who have ceased to bear children. But also before conception, the hare is healthy and the Magi give it to a man to drink. Likewise, nine grains of dung to a virgin so that the breasts may remain firm forever. Also with rennet. For this reason, smeared with honey, it is applied to blood where they do not want removed hair to grow back. For inflation of the womb, boar or pig dung smeared with oil is beneficial. It stops it more effectively if flour of the dried substance is sprinkled into a drink, so that it may alleviate the pains of a pregnant woman or a woman who has just given birth. When sow’s milk is drunk with honeyed wine, it aids the delivery of women. But when drunk by itself, it replenishes the failing breasts of women who have just given birth. The same, when smeared with female pig blood, makes them grow less. If they are painful, they are soothed by drinking donkey milk. When taken with added honey, it also aids their purgations. The aged tallow of the same animal heals ulcerations of the womb, and when applied on wool, it softens the hardness of the womb. By itself, fresh or aged, applied in water, it has the power of a <term>psilothrum</term> <gloss>depilatory agent</gloss>. The aged spleen of the same animal, applied in water, increases the supply of milk in the breasts. It clears the face. Fumigated donkey hooves hasten delivery, so that it might even induce an abortion, and it is used in no other way, as it kills the living fetus. If fresh dung of the same animal is applied, it is said to stop fluxes of blood in a marvelous way. And also the ash of the same dung, which, when applied, is beneficial for the womb. Horse foam applied for forty days prevents hair from growing before it starts. Likewise, stag horn is learned. It is better if the horns are fresh. The womb is aided by being washed with mare’s milk. If one senses the fetus is dead, the spleen, drunk in sweet water, expels it. Likewise, fumigation with hooves or dried dung. It stops sagging faces when infused with butter. Bull bile mixed with rose oil opens a hardened womb; it is applied externally on wool with turpentine resin. They also say that by the fumigation of dung from a bull, sagging wombs are restrained and delivery is aided. For conception, however, the drinking of cow’s milk. It is certain that sterility is caused by the exertion of childbirth. Olympias of Thebes affirms that this is corrected by bull bile and the fat of serpents, and with verdigris added to honey, applied to the affected parts before intercourse. It is also promised that if they eat calf meat roasted with birthwort around the time of conception, they will give birth to males. Calf marrow boiled in wine and water is beneficial with tallow for ulcerations of the womb. Likewise, fox fat and cat excrement applied with resin and rose oil. They believe that fumigating the womb with goat horn is most useful. The blood of wild goats with sea palm pulls out hair. The bile of others, however, when sprinkled on, softens the callous of the womb and causes conception after menstruation. In this way also, the power of a depilatory is made effective by being applied for three days after the hair is pulled out. Midwives promise that a flux, however immense, is stopped by drinking goat urine, and if the dung is applied topically. A goat membrane, aged and boiled in water, and taken as a drink in wine, expels the afterbirth. They think it useful to fumigate the womb with the hair of kids. And in a flux of blood, that rennet be drunk or henbane seed be applied. Aeschines says that if the loins of a woman are pricked with the blood of a wild black bull, a weariness of desire is induced. The same man says that goat urine, with spikenard added, is drunk for love. For infants, nothing is more useful than butter, by itself and with honey, especially during teething, and for the gums, and for sores of the mouth. A wolf’s tooth tied to an infant prevents terrors and the illnesses of teething. The wolf’s skin does the same. Their largest teeth, when tied to horses, are said to provide an indefatigable speed. The infant’s belly is stopped if rabbit rennet is applied to the breast. Donkey liver, with a little panacea instilled into the mouth, protects infants from epileptic diseases and others. They advise that this be done for forty days. And donkey skin thrown over them makes infants fearless. Teeth that fall out of horses first provide easy teething for infants when tied to them. More effectively if they have not touched the ground. Calf spleen is to be eaten in honey. And it is to be applied for pain of the spleen. For running sores, with honey. Calf spleen boiled in wine and ground up and applied to the small ulcers of the mouth. Goat brain passed through a gold ring before milk is given is instilled into the mouths of infants against epilepsy and other infant diseases. Goat dung tied in a cloth restrains restless infants, especially girls. Gums rubbed with goat milk or hare brain make for easy teething. Cato believes that sleep is induced if hare is taken in food. The common people also believe it grants grace to the body for nine days in the same place. Yet there must be some cause underlying such a great persuasion. The Magi say that the bile of a sacrificed goat, when applied strictly to the eyes or placed under the pillow, induces sleep. The ash of goat horn, when rubbed in with myrtle oil, inhibits sweat. Boar bile, when applied, stimulates intercourse. Likewise, the marrow of swine, when drunk. Donkey tallow mixed with the fat of a male goose, when applied.
